# ADK.Workflow.Checkpoint

Source: https://adk.hexdocs.pm/ADK.Workflow.Checkpoint.md

# `ADK.Workflow.Checkpoint`
[🔗](https://github.com/zeroasterisk/adk-elixir/blob/main/lib/adk/workflow/checkpoint.ex#L1)

Checkpoint behaviour for persisting workflow execution state.

Enables save/resume of workflow progress. Two implementations:

- `ADK.Workflow.Checkpoint.EtsStore` — fast in-process (default)
- `ADK.Workflow.Checkpoint.EctoStore` — durable database persistence

## Checkpoint Data

Each checkpoint captures:
- `workflow_id` — unique execution identifier
- `node_id` — the completed node
- `status` — `:completed`, `:failed`, `:running`
- `output` — node output data
- `timestamp` — when the checkpoint was taken

# `checkpoint`

```elixir
@type checkpoint() :: %{
  workflow_id: String.t(),
  node_id: node_id(),
  status: status(),
  output: any(),
  timestamp: DateTime.t()
}
```

# `node_id`

```elixir
@type node_id() :: atom() | String.t()
```

# `status`

```elixir
@type status() :: :completed | :failed | :running
```

# `clear`

```elixir
@callback clear(String.t()) :: :ok
```

Clear all checkpoints for a workflow execution.

# `completed_nodes`

```elixir
@callback completed_nodes(String.t()) :: [node_id()]
```

Get IDs of all completed nodes for a workflow.

# `load`

```elixir
@callback load(String.t(), node_id()) :: {:ok, checkpoint()} | :not_found
```

Load checkpoint for a specific node.

# `load_all`

```elixir
@callback load_all(String.t()) :: [checkpoint()]
```

Load all checkpoints for a workflow execution.

# `save`

```elixir
@callback save(String.t(), node_id(), status(), any()) :: :ok | {:error, term()}
```

Save a checkpoint for a completed node.

# `new`

```elixir
@spec new(String.t(), node_id(), status(), any()) :: checkpoint()
```

Create a checkpoint map.

# ADK.Workflow.Checkpoint.EctoStore

# `ADK.Workflow.Checkpoint.EctoStore`
[🔗](https://github.com/zeroasterisk/adk-elixir/blob/main/lib/adk/workflow/checkpoint/ecto_store.ex#L1)

Ecto-backed checkpoint store for durable workflow state persistence.

Requires an Ecto repo and a `workflow_checkpoints` table. This module
compiles unconditionally but operations require a running Ecto repo.

## Migration

    create table(:workflow_checkpoints) do
      add :workflow_id, :string, null: false
      add :node_id, :string, null: false
      add :status, :string, null: false
      add :output, :map
      timestamps()
    end

    create index(:workflow_checkpoints, [:workflow_id])
    create unique_index(:workflow_checkpoints, [:workflow_id, :node_id])

Requires Ecto as a dependency. Uses raw Ecto.Query for the lookup.

```elixir
@spec save_with_repo(module(), String.t(), atom() | String.t(), atom(), any()) ::
```

Save a checkpoint using the given Ecto repo.

# ADK.Workflow.Checkpoint.EtsStore

Source: https://adk.hexdocs.pm/ADK.Workflow.Checkpoint.EtsStore.md

# `ADK.Workflow.Checkpoint.EtsStore`
[🔗](https://github.com/zeroasterisk/adk-elixir/blob/main/lib/adk/workflow/checkpoint/ets_store.ex#L1)

ETS-backed checkpoint store for fast in-process workflow state persistence.

Uses a named ETS table owned by this GenServer, so the table persists even
when individual workflow executor processes die. Start in your supervision
tree or use `init/0` for ad-hoc use in tests.

## Supervision

    children = [
      ADK.Workflow.Checkpoint.EtsStore,
      # ...
    ]

Data is lost on VM restart (acceptable for development and short-lived
workflows). For durable persistence, use `ADK.Workflow.Checkpoint.EctoStore`.

# `child_spec`

Returns a specification to start this module under a supervisor.

See `Supervisor`.

# `init`

```elixir
@spec init() :: :ok
```

Initialize the ETS table for standalone/test use (no GenServer).
Idempotent and concurrent-safe.

# `start_link`

```elixir
@spec start_link(keyword()) :: GenServer.on_start()
```

Start the ETS owner process.

# ADK.Workflow.Collaboration

Source: https://adk.hexdocs.pm/ADK.Workflow.Collaboration.md

# `ADK.Workflow.Collaboration`
[🔗](https://github.com/zeroasterisk/adk-elixir/blob/main/lib/adk/workflow/collaboration.ex#L1)

Collaboration modes for workflow fan-out nodes.

When multiple agents process at a join point, the collaboration mode
determines how their outputs are combined.

## Modes

- `:pipeline` — output of each feeds into the next sequentially (default)
- `:debate` — all process same input, results are compared/synthesized
- `:vote` — all process same input, majority answer wins
- `:review` — first produces, subsequent review/critique the output

# `mode`

```elixir
@type mode() :: :pipeline | :debate | :vote | :review
```

# `result`

```elixir
@type result() :: %{events: [ADK.Event.t()], output: any()}
```

# `combine`

```elixir
@spec combine(mode(), [{String.t(), [ADK.Event.t()]}], ADK.Context.t()) :: result()
```

Combine results from multiple agents using the given collaboration mode.

## Parameters

- `mode` — collaboration strategy
- `results` — list of `{agent_name, events}` tuples from each agent
- `ctx` — the workflow context

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---

# ADK.Workflow.Executor

Source: https://adk.hexdocs.pm/ADK.Workflow.Executor.md

# `ADK.Workflow.Executor`
[🔗](https://github.com/zeroasterisk/adk-elixir/blob/main/lib/adk/workflow/executor.ex#L1)

Graph traversal and execution engine for workflows.

Traverses the DAG defined by `ADK.Workflow.Graph`, executing agent nodes and
routing based on context/events. Supports sequential traversal, parallel
fan-out with join, conditional routing, and checkpointing.

## Execution Model

1. Find `:START` edges → resolve initial nodes
2. Execute each node (agent or function)
3. Collect events, determine next nodes via edges
4. For fan-out: run parallel branches with `Task.async_stream`
5. For join: wait for all predecessors to complete
6. Checkpoint after each node completion
7. Terminate when `:END` is reached or no more nodes

## Telemetry

Emits `[:adk, :workflow, *]` telemetry events for FlowLive integration:
- `[:adk, :workflow, :start]` — workflow execution begins
- `[:adk, :workflow, :node, :start]` — node execution begins
- `[:adk, :workflow, :node, :stop]` — node execution completes
- `[:adk, :workflow, :stop]` — workflow execution completes

# `run_opts`

```elixir
@type run_opts() :: [
  checkpoint_store: module(),
  collaboration: ADK.Workflow.Collaboration.mode(),
  timeout: pos_integer(),
  node_timeout: pos_integer(),
  resume_id: String.t() | nil
]
```

# `run`

```elixir
@spec run(ADK.Workflow.Graph.t(), ADK.Context.t(), run_opts()) :: [ADK.Event.t()]
```

Execute a workflow graph.

## Options

- `:checkpoint_store` — checkpoint backend (default: `Checkpoint.EtsStore`)
- `:collaboration` — collaboration mode for fan-in (default: `:pipeline`)
- `:timeout` — global timeout in ms (default: 300_000)
- `:node_timeout` — per-node timeout in ms (default: 60_000)
- `:resume_id` — workflow ID to resume from checkpoints

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---

# ADK.Workflow.Graph

Source: https://adk.hexdocs.pm/ADK.Workflow.Graph.md

# `ADK.Workflow.Graph`
[🔗](https://github.com/zeroasterisk/adk-elixir/blob/main/lib/adk/workflow/graph.ex#L1)

Graph data structure for workflow definitions.

Represents a directed acyclic graph (DAG) of nodes and edges. Supports
unconditional edges, conditional routing (map-based), fan-out (parallel
branches), and fan-in (join nodes).

## Node Types

- Agent structs (any `ADK.Agent.t()`)
- Anonymous functions (`fn context -> events end`)
- `:START` / `:END` sentinel atoms

## Edge Types

- Unconditional: `{from, to}` — always traverse
- Conditional: `{from, %{"route_key" => to_node}}` — route based on context

# `edge`

```elixir
@type edge() ::
  {node_id(), node_id()} | {node_id(), %{required(String.t()) =&gt; node_id()}}
```

# `node_id`

```elixir
@type node_id() :: atom() | String.t()
```

# `t`

```elixir
@type t() :: %ADK.Workflow.Graph{
  edges: [edge()],
  nodes: %{required(node_id()) =&gt; any()}
}
```

# `build`

```elixir
@spec build([edge()], %{required(node_id()) =&gt; any()}) :: t()
```

Build a graph from edge tuples.

Edge tuples are `{from, to}` for unconditional or `{from, %{...}}` for conditional.
Nodes are extracted automatically from edges.

## Examples

    iex> g = ADK.Workflow.Graph.build([{:START, :a}, {:a, :END}], %{a: agent})
    iex> Map.keys(g.nodes) |> Enum.sort()
    [:END, :START, :a]

# `conditional_edges`

```elixir
@spec conditional_edges(t()) :: [{node_id(), %{required(String.t()) =&gt; node_id()}}]
```

Find edges that are conditional (map-based routing).

# `join_nodes`

```elixir
@spec join_nodes(t()) :: [node_id()]
```

Find nodes with multiple predecessors (join points).

# `outgoing`

```elixir
@spec outgoing(t(), node_id()) ::
  {:unconditional, [node_id()]}
  | {:conditional, %{required(String.t()) =&gt; node_id()}}
  | :none
```

Return the edge definition for a given source node.
Returns `{:unconditional, [targets]}` or `{:conditional, route_map}`.

# `predecessors`

```elixir
@spec predecessors(t(), node_id()) :: [node_id()]
```

Return predecessors of a node.

# `successors`

```elixir
@spec successors(t(), node_id()) :: [node_id()]
```

Return successors of a node. For conditional edges, returns all possible targets.

# `validate`

```elixir
@spec validate(t()) :: :ok | {:error, String.t()}
```

Validate the graph structure.

Checks:
- Has at least one `:START` edge
- All edge targets reference known nodes
- No cycles (DAG enforcement)
- No unreachable nodes (except `:START`)

Returns `:ok` or `{:error, reason}`.

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---

# ADK.Workflow.Graph.Mutation

# `ADK.Workflow.Graph.Mutation`
[🔗](https://github.com/zeroasterisk/adk-elixir/blob/main/lib/adk/workflow/graph/mutation.ex#L1)

Functional mutations for workflow graphs.

All operations return a new `%Graph{}` — the original is never modified.
Mutations validate the result (no cycles, no dangling edges).

Net-new: not present in Python ADK.

# `add_edge`

```elixir
@spec add_edge(ADK.Workflow.Graph.t(), ADK.Workflow.Graph.edge()) ::
  {:ok, ADK.Workflow.Graph.t()} | {:error, String.t()}
```

Add an edge to the graph. Validates no cycles and no dangling references.

# `add_node`

```elixir
@spec add_node(ADK.Workflow.Graph.t(), ADK.Workflow.Graph.node_id(), any()) ::
  {:ok, ADK.Workflow.Graph.t()} | {:error, String.t()}
```

Add a node to the graph.
Returns `{:ok, graph}` or `{:error, reason}`.

# `merge`

```elixir
@spec merge(ADK.Workflow.Graph.t(), ADK.Workflow.Graph.t()) ::
  {:ok, ADK.Workflow.Graph.t()} | {:error, String.t()}
```

Merge two graphs (union of nodes and edges).
Nodes in `graph2` override those in `graph1` on conflict.
Validates the merged result.

# `remove_edge`

```elixir
@spec remove_edge(
  ADK.Workflow.Graph.t(),
  ADK.Workflow.Graph.node_id(),
  ADK.Workflow.Graph.node_id()
) ::
  {:ok, ADK.Workflow.Graph.t()} | {:error, String.t()}
```

Remove an edge from the graph.

# `remove_node`

```elixir
@spec remove_node(ADK.Workflow.Graph.t(), ADK.Workflow.Graph.node_id()) ::
  {:ok, ADK.Workflow.Graph.t()} | {:error, String.t()}
```

Remove a node and all edges referencing it.
Returns `{:ok, graph}` or `{:error, reason}`.

# `replace_node`

```elixir
@spec replace_node(ADK.Workflow.Graph.t(), ADK.Workflow.Graph.node_id(), any()) ::
  {:ok, ADK.Workflow.Graph.t()} | {:error, String.t()}
```

Replace a node's definition, keeping all edges intact.

# ADK.Workflow.Graph.Runtime

# `ADK.Workflow.Graph.Runtime`
[🔗](https://github.com/zeroasterisk/adk-elixir/blob/main/lib/adk/workflow/graph/runtime.ex#L1)

GenServer that wraps a graph and allows atomic mutations during execution.

Maintains a history of graph states (up to 10) for undo/debugging.

Net-new: not present in Python ADK.

# `child_spec`

Returns a specification to start this module under a supervisor.

See `Supervisor`.

# `get`

```elixir
@spec get(GenServer.server()) :: ADK.Workflow.Graph.t()
```

Get the current graph.

# `history`

```elixir
@spec history(GenServer.server()) :: [ADK.Workflow.Graph.t()]
```

Return list of past graph states (most recent first).

# `mutate`

```elixir
@spec mutate(GenServer.server(), (ADK.Workflow.Graph.t() -&gt;
                              {:ok, ADK.Workflow.Graph.t()} | {:error, any()})) ::
  :ok | {:error, any()}
```

Apply a mutation function atomically.

The function receives the current graph and must return
`{:ok, new_graph}` or `{:error, reason}`.

# `rollback`

```elixir
@spec rollback(GenServer.server()) :: :ok | {:error, :no_history}
```

Rollback to the previous graph state.

# `start_link`

```elixir
@spec start_link(ADK.Workflow.Graph.t(), GenServer.options()) :: GenServer.on_start()
```

Start the runtime with an initial graph.

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

# ADK.Workflow.Graph.Validator

Source: https://adk.hexdocs.pm/ADK.Workflow.Graph.Validator.md

# `ADK.Workflow.Graph.Validator`
[🔗](https://github.com/zeroasterisk/adk-elixir/blob/main/lib/adk/workflow/graph/validator.ex#L1)

Validates workflow graph structure.

Net-new: not present in Python ADK.

# `acyclic?`

```elixir
@spec acyclic?(ADK.Workflow.Graph.t()) :: boolean()
```

Returns `true` if the graph has no cycles.
Uses DFS-based cycle detection.

# `validate`

```elixir
@spec validate(ADK.Workflow.Graph.t()) :: :ok | {:error, [String.t()]}
```

Validate the graph structure.

Checks:
- No cycles (DAG enforcement)
- All edge targets reference known nodes
- `:START` node exists with outgoing edges
- `:END` is reachable from `:START`
- No orphan nodes (unreachable from `:START`)

Returns `:ok` or `{:error, reasons}` where reasons is a list of strings.

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---

# ADK.Workflow.Retry

Source: https://adk.hexdocs.pm/ADK.Workflow.Retry.md

# `ADK.Workflow.Retry`
[🔗](https://github.com/zeroasterisk/adk-elixir/blob/main/lib/adk/workflow/retry.ex#L1)

Per-node retry logic for workflow steps.

Wraps node execution with configurable retry count and backoff strategy.
Retries are attempted when the node returns `{:error, _}` or raises an exception.

## Backoff Strategies

- `:exponential` — `100ms * 2^attempt` (100, 200, 400, 800, ...)
- `:linear` — `100ms * attempt` (100, 200, 300, ...)
- integer — fixed delay in milliseconds (e.g., `500` → 500ms between each retry)

## Telemetry

Emits `[:adk, :workflow, :node, :retry]` on each retry attempt with metadata:
- `:workflow_id`, `:node_id`, `:attempt`, `:max_retries`, `:backoff_ms`, `:reason`

# `backoff_delay`

```elixir
@spec backoff_delay(:exponential | :linear | pos_integer(), non_neg_integer()) ::
  non_neg_integer()
```

Calculate backoff delay in milliseconds for a given attempt (0-indexed).

# `with_retry`

```elixir
@spec with_retry(
  fun :: (-&gt; {atom() | {:error, any()}, list(), any()}),
  retry_times :: non_neg_integer(),
  backoff :: :exponential | :linear | pos_integer(),
  meta :: map()
) :: {atom() | {:error, any()}, list(), any()}
```

Execute `fun` with retry logic.

`fun` is a zero-arity function that returns `{status, events, output}`.
If `status` is not `:ok`, retries up to `retry_times` with the given `backoff`.

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---

# ADK.Workflow.Step

Source: https://adk.hexdocs.pm/ADK.Workflow.Step.md

# `ADK.Workflow.Step`
[🔗](https://github.com/zeroasterisk/adk-elixir/blob/main/lib/adk/workflow/step.ex#L1)

Represents a single workflow step with support for execution and compensation.

# `backoff`

```elixir
@type backoff() :: :exponential | :linear | pos_integer()
```

# `t`

```elixir
@type t() :: %ADK.Workflow.Step{
  backoff: backoff(),
  compensate: (any(), any(), any() -&gt; any()) | nil,
  name: atom() | String.t(),
  retry_times: non_neg_integer(),
  run: (any() -&gt; any()) | (any(), any() -&gt; any()),
  validate:
    (any(), any() -&gt; :ok | {:error, any()})
    | (any() -&gt; :ok | {:error, any()})
    | nil
}
```

# `new`

```elixir
@spec new(atom() | String.t(), function(), function() | nil, function() | nil) :: t()
```

Create a new step with a run function and optional compensation function.

## Options

- `:compensate` — compensation function for saga rollback
- `:validate` — validation function for output
- `:retry_times` — max retry attempts on failure (default: 0)
- `:backoff` — backoff strategy: `:exponential`, `:linear`, or fixed ms (default: `:exponential`)

# `new_with_opts`

```elixir
@spec new_with_opts(atom() | String.t(), function(), keyword()) :: t()
```

Create a new step with keyword options for full configuration.

## Examples

    Step.new_with_opts(:fetch, &fetch/1, retry_times: 3, backoff: :exponential)
    Step.new_with_opts(:save, &save/1, retry_times: 2, backoff: 500)

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

# mix adk.doctor

Source: https://adk.hexdocs.pm/Mix.Tasks.Adk.Doctor.md

# `mix adk.doctor`
[🔗](https://github.com/zeroasterisk/adk-elixir/blob/main/lib/mix/tasks/adk.doctor.ex#L1)

Validates your environment for ADK Elixir development.

Checks Elixir/OTP versions, API keys, dependencies, and agent modules
to help diagnose common setup issues.

## Usage

    mix adk.doctor
    mix adk.doctor --verbose
    mix adk.doctor --json

## Options

  * `--verbose` — Show additional detail for each check
  * `--json` — Output results as JSON (for CI/tooling)

## Checks

  * Elixir version (>= 1.15 required, >= 1.16 recommended)
  * OTP version (>= 25 required, >= 26 recommended)
  * GEMINI_API_KEY / GOOGLE_API_KEY environment variables
  * ADK dependency present in project
  * Optional dependencies (Phoenix/Plug, Protobuf)
  * Agent modules implementing ADK.Agent behaviour

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---
